• Walls of alimentary canal have the same four basic tissue layers

• Epithelium that covers surface of lumen
• Secretes mucus, digestive enzymes, and hormones
• Absorbs end products of digestion
• Protects against infectious disease
• Submucosa
• Connective tissue
• Contains blood and lymphatic vessels, and nerve plexus

• Inner circular layer and outer longitudinal layer of smooth muscle tissue for per

• Connects to esophagus and trachea

• Defecation 1. Feces movements toward rectum by peristalsis Distension of rectal wall triggers defecation reflex 2. Parasympathetic signals stimulate contraction of sigmoid colon and rectum Relaxation of internal anal sphincter 3. • Aging and the digestive system
• GI tract activity declines with age
• produces less digestive juice;
• absorption is less efficient;
• peristalsis slows, causing decline in frequency of bowel movements
• Taste/smell becomes less acute; periodontal disease often develops
• Constipation, fecal incontinence, and cancer of GI tract are fairly common
• Prevention: regular dental and medical examinations

Anatomy of Digestive System
• Small intestine ○ Small intestine’s length and other structural modifications provide huge surface area for nutrient absorption ○ Modifications include
• Circular folds
• Villi
• Microvilli

Anatomy of Digestive System
• Circular folds
• ~1 cm deep folds that force chyme to pass slowly through lumen, allowing more time for absorption
• Villi
• ~1 mm high fingerlike projections of mucosa
• contains dense capillary bed and lymphatic capillary called lacteal for absorption
• Microvilli
• Extensions of mucosal cell’s plasma membrane that give fuzzy microscopic appearance called the brush border
• contains brush border enzymes for final digestion of carbohydrate and protein

Anatomy of Digestive System
• Large intestine
• Does not contain circular folds, villi, or digestive secretions
• Contains many mucus-producing goblet cells
• Residue remains in large intestine 12–24 hours
• No food breakdown occurs except what enteric bacteria digest
• Vitamins (made by bacterial flora), water, and electrolytes (especially Na + and Cl − ) are absorbed
• Major functions of large intestine is propulsion of feces to anus and defecation
